title: The Door reads the body behind a locator inside its scope, as MACHINE_PROTOCOL version 2
summary: @inventarch/runtime: the Door accepts a new operation, read, with params {within?, locator, includeRuntime?}, and answers {ok: true, result} with the ReadBody readBody returns ({locator, identity, kind, path?, digest, body, certified: false}) or that function's read refusal. It always reads through a scope token, the initial boundary when within is omitted, so a locator that no admitted record in the scope answers, whether its record is outside the scope, refused by admission or absent, is one plain IA-RUNTIME-READ-UNADMITTED, 'The locator is not in this scope', which names no path, line, identity or refused record. The door reads documents through the new DoorOptions.read, by default @inventarch/db readWorkspaceBytes over its root bounded at 4 MiB, and binds adopted mounts once, when it opens, from .ia/workspace.json, unless it was opened with explicit adopted captures, which name no directory. The new DoorOptions.protocol is the MACHINE_PROTOCOL version a door serves, by default the current one: a door at version 1 refuses read as the unknown operation 1.1.0 refused, byte for byte, and a value that is not an integer from 1 to the current version is a TypeError. ReadBodyOptions gains an optional within: given a scope token, readBody reads get and records in that scope and refuses every miss with that plain refusal; without it readBody is unchanged. MACHINE_PROTOCOL is version 2: ProtocolOperation gains an optional since, absent on the nine version 1 rows, whose JSON is byte-identical to 1.1.0's; the read row is appended with since: 2 and mcp: ia_read, and flow gains one line. Code that expects MACHINE_PROTOCOL.version to be 1, or reads every row as a CLI machine route, should filter the rows by since. A version 2 door's unknown-operation refusal lists read last among the operations it admits. @inventarch/db exports readWorkspaceBytes(root, path, limit), which returns one workspace file's exact bytes and refuses a path that escapes the workspace, is not portable by the rule the distribution workspace file reader applies (NFC, at most 1024 code units, no backslash, control character or any of <>:"|?*, no segment that ends in a dot or a space or names a reserved device) or passes a link or junction, and a hard-linked or nonregular file (IA-DB-PATH-UNSAFE), a missing or unreadable file or one of more than limit bytes (IA-DB-SOURCE-UNAVAILABLE), and a file replaced or resized during the read (IA-DB-SOURCE-CHANGED); each refusal names the file by its canonical path alone. @inventarch/mcp-door serves a tenth tool, ia_read, whose inputSchema is the read row's params. @inventarch/cli: runCli, the machine route that @inventarch/cli/internal/main exports and the host launcher's door mode calls, opens its door at protocol version 1, so read there is refused with exactly 1.1.0's bytes; in @inventarch/cli/internal/operation-help, describeOperation describes only the version 1 rows, and renderOperationSchema and renderOperationHelp label a description version 1, as 1.1.0 did, whatever the table's version. Limits: the CLI's machine routes stay the nine version 1 operations, so ia scope in every form, the other routes, their help and their --schema output are unchanged, and ia read stays the consumer verb, which returns the Door's body and digest and refuses a document the Door refuses with the same code; the Door has no position operation yet.
